Description: Arduino Nano v3 (ATmega328P), on 2 x 15 female headers
Bulk capacitor, 12 V rail, 105 C electrolytic
Ceramic or MKT 100 nF: decoupling (C2, C3, C6, C9, C11) and button filter (C7)
Electrolytic: 5 V rail at U1 (C4), relay header (C10)
Flow signal filter capacitor
Receiver supply filter, electrolytic
Reverse-polarity crowbar: conducts and blows F1 if the supply is reversed
Flyback diode across the valve terminals, stripe (K) to valve +
25 L limit indicator, 5 mm
50 L limit indicator, 5 mm
100 L limit indicator, 5 mm
5x20 mm fuse holder + 2 A slow-blow fuse
12 V DC supply input, 2-way 5.08 mm screw terminal
Valve power out: 1 = +12V (fused) to relay COM, 2 = GND from valve -
Relay module header: 1 = VCC (+5V), 2 = IN (D8), 3 = GND
Flow sensor: 1 = +5V (red), 2 = SIG (yellow), 3 = GND (black)
ESP header: 1 = +5V, 2 = DATA (3.3 V level, to ESP RX), 3 = GND
Pull-ups: flow signal (R1), button (R3)
Series resistors: flow signal (R2), remote channels (R7-R10)
LED current limit, about 9 mA
ESP data divider (top)
ESP data divider (bottom), 5 V -> 3.24 V
Remote channel pull-down
Receiver supply filter resistor
Momentary push button (or panel button wired to these pads)
5 V regulator, TO-220 pinout IN-GND-OUT (L7805 + heatsink, or pin-compatible switcher R-78E5.0-1.0)
RX480E-4 receiver module on a 1x7 female header. Pins: 1 GND, 2 +V, 3-6 D0-D3, 7 VT
Sockets so the Nano can be unplugged
Only needed with an L7805
